domain: Whether the standardization of shipping containers caused the collapse of dockworker unions, or whether declining union power let the box's standard dimensions win out over rival designs
topic: Whether the standardization of shipping containers caused the collapse of dockworker unions, or whether declining union power let the box's standard dimensions win out over rival designs

movement.gist: Tell the textbook story: Malcom McLean's steel box, adopted in the 1950s-60s, made cargo handling so efficient that it broke the longshoremen's unions by eliminating the labor they controlled — technology first, union decline after.

Introduce archival detail: the ILWU and other dockworker unions had already negotiated mechanization agreements and were losing bargaining leverage over cargo-handling rules years before any single container standard was settled on; multiple incompatible box sizes competed through the 1960s while union power was already eroding port by port.

Argue that the standard (ISO container dimensions, fixed only after prolonged industry battles) and union collapse are the same process seen from two sides: weakened unions could no longer force shipping lines to accommodate varied box sizes tied to differing work rules, and it was precisely that lack of resistance that let one dimension win — each caused the other's advance in the same years, not in sequence.

Concede that this mutual-causation picture cannot be fully verified port-by-port or extended to standardization generally — hold the claim to its narrow, evidenced scope: only for the specific case of container-size convergence and dockworker bargaining power in this period does the arrow of causation genuinely suspend; elsewhere the standard sequence may hold.

primary.axis: which came first: the technical standard (a single container size) or the institutional weakness (unions unable to resist it)
poles: the box's efficiency forced the ports and unions to adapt
union fragmentation is what let one box design defeat its rivals, not the other way round

secondary.axis: whether standardization itself is a technical fact or a labor-political outcome dressed up as one
poles: standard sizes are neutral engineering optima
standard sizes are the fossilized record of who lost a bargaining fight

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension supplies the mechanism by which the primary's arrow gets suspended: if the standard itself is political, asking 'which caused which' becomes the wrong question at the wrong scale

family_realization.note: Passage executes simultaneity with precision. Paragraph 2 denies box-first ('shrink through late 1950s, before any single box'). Paragraph 3 collapses arrow: 'Each advance cleared ground for the other in the same span of months.' Perfect temporal-order distraction reversal.

ending_behavior.note: Final paragraph performs 'Narrowed Claim' masterfully. Thesis survives only 'for a narrow object only...between 1956 and 1970, on coasts where contracts can be read.' Aperture narrows visibly. Closing: 'suspension...not a refusal to decide' — refusal suspended. Exact intent.

voice_consistency.note: Cold Enthusiast throughout. 'the hook and controlled the pace' — concrete particular. Uneven: 'the union hall on the waterfront' (lyrical) shifts to archive-dense syntax. Fascination audible under flat delivery. Minor: one or two sentences edge toward formula.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(A): example_promotion — strong reader tempted by paragraph 1's opening. Q2(C): example_promotion — same trap. Q3(C): causal_inversion — plausible misread of 'starting gun.' Q6(A): half_truth — summary accuracy masks argumentative purpose. Traps earned.

explanation_quality.note: Every wrong option tied to passage mechanism. Q1(D): 'expressly disowns this general theory' (para 4, line exact). Q5(A): 'No such invention claim appears.' Q8(B): 'entanglement claim built in para 3; para 4 restricts scope.' Specific, locatable.

answers.reasoning: Passage argues entangled simultaneity, not sequential causation, explicitly stated in paragraph three.
Text explicitly states neither arrow points; both are the same line seen twice.
Passage states standardization was 'an outcome still years away' while decline was already occurring.
Supports coupling of manning rules with varied sizes, confirming the claim about weakened union enabling standardization.
Passage explicitly notes ILA leverage eroded before any single box existed to blame.
Shows no single standardized box existed early enough to be the trigger; B also plausible as transition device.
Passage states sequence collapses into simultaneity, so causal question loses footing, per final paragraph.
Fourth paragraph explicitly limits scope; removing it would remove that boundary, inviting overgeneralization.
